contract: Pure policy for a new message during a Run under the one declared rule (queue, reject, interrupt, steer or side run) and the supplied Run phase: deliver, queue up to 16, refuse, or interrupt or hand to a side run with a report of delivered and open actions; every other input passes. No runtime, Run start or stop.
limits: No process, clock, timer, storage, callback or recording; it does not start, cancel or stop a Run or an action, and adds no input kind that carries the report to a pattern.
The report names actions with an applied outcome and open actions in pattern-step terms only; it does not say what a person has seen nor that an open action was not sent.
Selected Cure law covers supplied classifications only; map validation, the queue and the Run facts are finite-test grounded.
Phase and when new work may start stay with workflow/bot-run-lifecycle; Attempt currentness stays with workflow/run; no child-Run action in v1.

grounding.claim: For each rule, phase and queue fill class, an input that is not a message gives the pass decision; excludes map validation, the queue contents and the Run facts.
Pinned Cure checks types and totality of the production decision table; the source audit reports no axiom, hole, unresolved, unaudited, opaque or unproved-total definition and zero absurd.

Named groups wake_bypasses_every_rule, five_rules_one_trace and side_run_leaves_first_run_unchanged, redacted invalid operands, the Cure law/audit and the checked example pass; letting a side-run message enter the queue makes side_run_leaves_first_run_unchanged fail (negative control). Finite scenarios.
Pinned Cure compilation, reduction checking and BEAM decision semantics; compiler soundness not locally proved.
Pinned Elixir immutable maps and lists; ready PatternStep decode/encode is reused unchanged.

The caller supplies truthful Run facts (the phase that bot-run-lifecycle decided for the same input, delivered and open action IDs), records each input before the policy reads it, gives only current-Attempt inputs, calls next only when new work is permitted, handles interrupts and side runs under the Run and lifecycle rules, and serializes and preserves the state.

telemetry.contract: Pure callable emits no observations; the host owns instrumentation.

config.contract: The rule (queue, reject, interrupt, steer or side_run) is a caller choice set when the state is constructed for one Run and passed with every call; it never changes during the Run and there is no hot reconfiguration. The queue bound of 16 is fixed, not Config.

control.contract: No independently controlled runtime or lifecycle commands; interrupt and side run are decisions for the caller.
